open_from_reviewers_not_yet_fixed: B6 root cause: makeHeightField forces height to zero within 30 m of every point on the circuit, so the whole flight area is a plane and there is nothing between a 250 mm quad and a 200 m mountain
B2: shadow acne on the tree canopies, and each canopy blob carries its own inverted hull so one tree reads as four outlined balloons
B2: the lake plane cuts trees and rocks with no waterline treatment, and a flag pole with its cloth passes through a tree canopy

B4: water is a constant band ramp with no light model and every band is cool, including the lit crests; its depth bands are keyed to radius from the lake centre rather than to depth, so from altitude it will read as a bullseye
B4 and B1: the rim term in celmat.js is step(0.5, rim) with no sun term, so it floods whole grazing angle faces with a cool grey wash and is brightest on the shadow side
B1: the lake's shoreline foam is a 12 m band pinned to the disc radius rather than to the waterline, and it is the second brightest thing in the world
B4: SUN_DIR is close to co-axial with the start line view, so the four band ramp delivers only a 1.38 to 1 spread across a whole tree canopy and there is no terminator to judge
B5: the amber accent is used for the gate rings, the OSD gate counter, the banner, every settings heading and the throttle bar, so the colour that means gate does not only mean gate
B1 and B6: the 70 m cream sand shore, one flat value with no detail
B6: mountain ring 3 reaches 1515 m while the sky dome is a 1500 m sphere, so its outer slivers are overpainted
gates 2 to 8 use red orange bands while the tutorial text says to chase the amber rings
performance: 204 static gate meshes and 72 flag cloths are 77 percent of the draw calls, and the merger is already in the same file
performance: the grass fragment shader spends 16 shadow map compares and 12 noise hashes per fragment on two values that cannot vary across a 3 cm blade
performance: antialias true costs about 118 MB at 1440p and delivers nothing, because EffectComposer allocates its own non multisampled targets, so the frame has no antialiasing at all
performance: grass.frustumCulled false submits 552000 triangles and 32 MB of vertex buffer every frame regardless of view
performance: load is a 2195 ms synchronous stall, dominated by 67 million distance to track evaluations
performance: the attract view is 701 draw calls against 237 in flight, and the round 4 increase of 9 percent is unaccounted for
C1 to C5 untouched: no latency measurement, no ground effect, no impact feedback, audio is still a sawtooth per motor
